data.body:
RESEARCH_FINDINGS (cross-runner equivalence — accepted community practice; gathered during /dso:brainstorm)

Question: when multiple test-execution harnesses must agree on how they classify the same test (pass/fail/skip) and have drifted on edge cases (expected-failure markers, timeouts, scope), what is accepted practice to prevent/catch the drift?

1. Single-oracle model is universal (not pairwise). CommonMark spec.txt and the JSON Schema Test Suite bake an (input, expected-output) pair into each static corpus case; every implementation is validated independently against that oracle, never compared pairwise. Avoids N x (N-1) explosion; ground truth is version-controlled independently of any harness; adding an implementation = point it at the corpus.
   Sources: https://github.com/commonmark/commonmark-spec ; https://github.com/json-schema-org/JSON-Schema-Test-Suite

2. Per-test metadata drives skip/xfail classification (test262). Each test carries YAML frontmatter declaring negative.phase/negative.type (expected error), flags, and features (capability tokens); a harness skips/xfails tests whose features it does not support. Expected-failure and skip are first-class CORPUS properties, not harness-side policy — which is exactly what prevents cross-harness drift.
   Source: https://github.com/tc39/test262/blob/main/INTERPRETING.md

3. Inline scope directives for partial-overlap engines (SQLLogicTest). A reference run materializes expected results; other engines validate against that file. Per-engine differences handled by inline skipif <engine> / onlyif <engine> directives embedded in the corpus, not the harness. Unit of comparison = the materialized script; every engine must match for every non-gated case.
   Source: https://sqlite.org/sqllogictest/doc/trunk/about.wiki

4. Regression corpus as a ratchet (xfail-to-permanent-fixture). On a divergence: commit a minimal reproducer to the corpus immediately (xfail/skipif), then remove the marker when fixed so it becomes a permanent passing fixture annotated with the divergence ID. Directly maps to SC5 (cited drift tickets become regression cases).
   Source: https://blog.ganssle.io/articles/2021/11/pytest-xfail.html

5. CI is the authoritative gate; path-filtered trigger is the recognized pattern. GitHub Actions paths: filtering (e.g. runners/**, harness/**, corpus/**) runs the equivalence suite only when runner/harness/corpus code changes; pre-commit and CI must call the IDENTICAL script to avoid context drift.
   Sources: https://github.com/dorny/paths-filter ; https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=29635885

Synthesis / design implication: adopt the single-oracle model (each corpus case carries its own canonical pass/fail/skip verdict) plus a per-case scope annotation declaring which harnesses it applies to (test262 features / sqllogictest skipif style). Cross-runner equivalence = for every case in the INTERSECTION of two harnesses' scopes, both must produce the oracle verdict; out-of-scope cases report 'out of scope', not pass/fail. This is O(N), auto-extends to new harnesses via the manifest, and dissolves the partial-overlap problem (the four bash-capable harnesses vs the disjoint node/pytest drivers). Gate placement: CI authoritative on a paths: filter, with the same script reused by the pre-commit hook.

Note: the original SC4 framing ("runners declared in plugins/dso/scripts/runners/") should be corrected — that directory holds the language drivers (bash/node/pytest); the four drifting harnesses (bash-runner.sh, tests/lib/suite-engine.sh, tests/hooks/run-hook-tests.sh, plugins/dso/scripts/validate.sh) live in several locations and should be enumerated by the manifest, not the directory.
